Keep the room modest and vague; do not invent a missing person's identity, financial cause, hospital or new evidence. BOTTOM LEFT (frame 4): Back in the woman's care room, her shoulders have lowered and the braced free hand now rests loosely on her thigh. She listens into an ordinary-sized receiver, mouth closed before a softer reply, eyes showing recognition rather than triumph. The husband remains resting in the same bed, reminding us that her burden continues. The exaggerated shadow has thinned into an ordinary telephone shadow. Keep her face and actual connected fingers readable; no sudden smile that erases the day. BOTTOM RIGHT (frame 5): Return to the two separate rooms in quiet balanced proportions, divided clearly and softly, not joined. The woman sits near her resting husband with a relaxed telephone grip; the caller sits alone at his own table, shoulders a little less defensive. Both receivers are ordinary, both faces tired but less hardened. Keep the distinct sage and mauve clothing and each room's unchanged furniture.
